svg.title: What Are Streams?
svg.desc: Auto-playing 64s step-by-step explainer of "What Are Streams?" (from img_11.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: Process data piece by piece (chunks) without completing the whole read or write and without keeping all the data in memory
Use it, send it, drop it

g.text: What: Streams read and write data piece by piece (chunks), without finishing the whole
operation first and without keeping all the data in memory.
Why: Perfect for large data (videos, logs, uploads): less memory and less waiting. Netflix
Added: Backpressure (a slow writer pausing a fast reader) and highWaterMark (chunk size).
wait for ALL, hold ALL in RAM
start now, hold one chunk at a time
What: Big files and network data are often far larger than you want in memory at once.
Added: Each chunk is a Buffer (raw bytes), unless you set an encoding like 'utf8'.
What: fs.readFile reads the entire file into memory and only then gives it to you.
Why: 100 users downloading a 2 GB video at once = 200 GB of RAM. The server dies.
What: A read stream hands you the file 64 KB at a time. Each chunk is sent and then
Why: Memory use stays small and steady no matter how big the file is.
file.pipe(res); // send each chunk as it arrives
// RAM ≈ a few chunks per user, any file size
What: You don't have to wait until all the data is available: processing starts with the
Why: The video starts playing while the rest is still downloading.
for await (const line of rl) { // line by line
} // first error shows long before the file ends
What: If data is read faster than it can be written (disk → slow network), chunks pile up in
memory. Backpressure pauses the reader until the writer catches up.
Why: Without it, streams can use as much memory as readFile, or more.
// pipe() / pipeline() do exactly this for you
What: highWaterMark sets how much a stream buffers before it applies backpressure, so it is
Why: Smaller = less memory but more callbacks; bigger = fewer callbacks but more memory per
What: Streams = data in chunks: low memory and a fast start. Ideal for videos, big files,
Added: Chunks are Buffers, backpressure (write() → false, drain), highWaterMark chunk size,
readFile(2 GB) → ~2 GB RAM, starts after full read
createReadStream(2 GB) → ~64 KB RAM, starts immediately

svg.text: Streams = data in chunks, low memory
readFile on huge files inside a server
Q: What is backpressure in streams?
A: Pausing the reader until the writer drains
